seo.metaDescription: Stat, Delta, Meter, RangeMeter, ZoneMeter, InlineBar, DotCount, Sparkline, ShareBar, Legend and TooltipPill: the HTML pieces around your charts.

props.markdown: The small pieces are the numbers and meters around your charts: a headline figure, a progress bar, a count of dots, a legend. They are plain HTML and CSS (`Sparkline` is the one exception, a single stretched `<svg>`), they read the same `--ch-*` tokens as the charts, and you can use them anywhere on a page, in a table cell or a dashboard card, without a `Chart` around them.

The only two that belong with a chart are `Legend`, which explains what a chart's colors and shapes mean, and `TooltipPill`, which is what a `Tooltip` shows. Numbers are formatted with the locale and currency of the nearest `ChartsProvider`, see [Hooks and providers](/docs/hooks-and-providers).

`Stat` is a headline number with a label, a change and a caption. `Delta` is the change: an arrow and the size of the move, colored by whether it is good news (`good="down"` for cost). `InlineBar` and `DotCount` fit in a table cell: a bar against a scale with an optional target tick, and a count drawn as dots.

Every element that carries meaning has text for screen readers. `Delta` says "Up" or "Down" before the number, `InlineBar` gets an accessible name from its `label`, and `DotCount` keeps the full count readable even when it draws fewer dots than `max`. None of the props are functions, so this example also renders in a Server Component.

Colored text in the small pieces, such as a toned value, mixes the tone with `--ch-ink` so that it stays readable. `--ch-tone-text-mix` is the share of the tone in that mix, 55% by default; see [Theming](/docs/theming).

`Sparkline` is a line of values for a KPI row or a table cell. It has no axes, no tooltip and no tab stop, and it fills the width of its container at a fixed `height` (28 px by default). A `null` breaks the line, `area` adds a soft fill, `target` draws a thin rule and `endpoint` puts a dot on the last value. The dot is an HTML element positioned in percent, so it stays round at any width. Without `domain` the scale spans the values and the target, and a flat series sits at mid height. With no value at all, the accessible name becomes `label: No data`.

`Meter` shows progress toward a target. `RangeMeter` puts the actual value and the plan on one track, with a hatched gap between them. `ZoneMeter` colors the track in zones, here good, needs work and poor, and marks the value. `ShareBar` splits a whole into parts and lists them underneath.

`ZoneMeter` takes the zones as `{ bins, inclusive }`, which is the shape `thresholds()` returns, so you can pass its result straight in or write the plain object, as here, when the page is a Server Component. Each meter has a `label` that becomes its accessible name.

`ShareBar` draws one bar split by `value / total`, in the order of `segments`, with a list of the parts underneath ("2,711 · 46%"). `legendValue` is `'both'`, `'value'` or `'percent'`, and `legend={false}` keeps only the bar. A `total` larger than the sum of the parts leaves the rest as empty track.

- The percents in the list add up to 100.
- A part that rounds to 0% reads "<1%" and stays visible in the bar as a 3px sliver.
- Segments without a `tone` take `accent`, `accent-soft`, `warn`, `neutral` and `gain` in turn, and never `loss`: pink is only ever chosen explicitly.

`Legend` is a list of swatches next to a chart. Each item picks a `tone` and a `shape` (`bar`, `dot`, `line` or `band`), and a line can be `dashed`. `TooltipPill` is the segmented pill inside a `Tooltip`; the `content` function returns one for the hovered or focused point. A `line` swatch takes `marker: 'dot'` or `'ring'` for the points of the series, and a `band` swatch shows the soft fill of a `Band`.
`content` is a function, so this example is a client file. Hover a bar or focus the chart and use the arrow keys to see the pill.

**Almost no `<svg>` in these.** The small pieces are built from `div` and `span` elements, so they work in any layout, print cleanly and need no size. `Sparkline` draws one `<svg>` that fills its container, so it needs a box with a width, but it never measures it. Only a chart needs a width and a height.
